title: Ruddit: Norms of Offensiveness for English Reddit Comments
measurement_description: The paper measures the degree of offensiveness of Reddit comments using a fine-grained, real-valued scoring system. In relation to religion, it analyzes the association of specific identity terms (including religious groups) with offensiveness scores using Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI). It also evaluates whether computational models (BERT, HateBERT, BiLSTM) rely on these identity terms to predict offensiveness by comparing performance on the original dataset versus an 'identity-agnostic' version where terms are masked.
findings: The study found that certain religious identity terms, specifically 'muslim', exhibited a high association with offensive comments (high PMI with offensive score bins). Despite this dataset bias where religious terms appeared more frequently in offensive contexts, masking these identity terms (identity-agnostic dataset) did not substantially change the performance of the models (HateBERT, BERT, BiLSTM), suggesting the models were not solely relying on the presence of these terms to predict offensiveness scores.
